collection.name: PlantMetWiki SPARQL examples
collection.description: Example SPARQL queries for the PlantMetWiki SPARQL endpoint, shown in the SPARQL Explorer at https://plantmetwiki.bioinformatics.nl/.

examples.label: Number of pathways per species
examples.description: Count pathways per species, using DataNode-level species annotations.

examples.label: Number of entities per type
examples.description: Count all major entity types in PlantMetWiki.

examples.label: Triples per named graph
examples.description: Count triples per named graph in the PlantMetWiki triplestore.
examples.query:
# Named graphs:
#   graph/pathways              — core WikiPathways RDF (pathways + reactions)
#   graph/gpml-taxonomy-extra   — per-entity species annotations (wp:organism)
#   graph/gpml-properties-extra — PlantCyc key-value properties
#   graph/bgc-mibig             — MIBiG curated biosynthetic gene clusters
#   graph/bgc-plantismash       — plantiSMASH predicted biosynthetic gene clusters
#   graph/ncbitaxon             — NCBITaxon ontology (OBO Foundry, CC0)
#   graph/vocabularies          — pmw:/wp:/gpml: term definitions (self-describing schema)
#   void                        — VoID metadata for all datasets

# Uses VALUES to enumerate only the known PlantMetWiki graphs — fast because
# Virtuoso can use per-graph statistics instead of scanning every triple.
# (A FILTER on ?graph after GRAPH ?g { ?s ?p ?o } forces a full scan of all
# graphs including the 21.7M-triple NCBITaxon graph before filtering.)

SELECT ?graph (COUNT(*) AS ?nTriples)
WHERE {
  VALUES ?graph {
    <http://rdf-plantmetwiki.bioinformatics.nl/graph/pathways>
    <http://rdf-plantmetwiki.bioinformatics.nl/graph/gpml-taxonomy-extra>
    <http://rdf-plantmetwiki.bioinformatics.nl/graph/gpml-properties-extra>
    <http://rdf-plantmetwiki.bioinformatics.nl/graph/bgc-plantismash>
    <http://rdf-plantmetwiki.bioinformatics.nl/graph/bgc-mibig>
    <http://rdf-plantmetwiki.bioinformatics.nl/graph/ncbitaxon>
    <http://rdf-plantmetwiki.bioinformatics.nl/graph/vocabularies>
    <http://rdf-plantmetwiki.bioinformatics.nl/void>
  }
  GRAPH ?graph { ?s ?p ?o . }
}
GROUP BY ?graph
ORDER BY DESC(?nTriples)

examples.label: Taxa missing from NCBITaxon
examples.description: Find taxa in PlantMetWiki that cannot be resolved to a label in the local NCBITaxon ontology graph (graph/ncbitaxon).
examples.query:
# Even with the full OBO Foundry NCBITaxon release loaded, some taxa may be
# absent because:
#   - The NCBI taxon ID has been deprecated/merged (e.g. NCBITaxon_283673
#     = Lycopersicon hirsutum, now merged into Solanum habrochaites NCBI 62890)
#   - The OBO Foundry release does not include every NCBI taxon (it focuses
#     on biologically relevant taxa used in ontology annotation)
#
# Results for PlantCyc 17.0 with the full NCBITaxon release (v2026-05-13):
#   6 unresolvable taxa · 54 affected GeneProduct/Protein nodes
#   (all are gene/enzyme annotations, no metabolites affected)
#
# Columns:
#   ?taxon      — the unresolved OBO Foundry IRI
#   ?ncbiID     — numeric NCBI Taxonomy ID (extracted from IRI)
#   ?nNodes     — number of GeneProduct/Protein nodes with this taxon
#   ?nodeTypes  — entity types (GeneProduct, Protein)
#
# Look up deprecated/merged taxa:
#   https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/Taxonomy/Browser/wwwtax.cgi?id=<ncbiID>

PREFIX wp:      <http://vocabularies.wikipathways.org/wp#>
PREFIX ncbi:    <http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/NCBITaxon_>
PREFIX rdfs:    <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#>
PREFIX dcterms: <http://purl.org/dc/terms/>

SELECT ?taxon
       (STRAFTER(STR(?taxon), "NCBITaxon_") AS ?ncbiID)
       (COUNT(DISTINCT ?node) AS ?nNodes)
       (GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT STRAFTER(STR(?nodeType), "wp#"); separator=", ") AS ?nodeTypes)
WHERE {
  # Step 1: collect all species-specific taxa from our taxonomy annotations
  GRAPH <http://rdf-plantmetwiki.bioinformatics.nl/graph/gpml-taxonomy-extra> {
    ?node wp:organism ?taxon .
    FILTER(?taxon != ncbi:33090)  # exclude Viridiplantae (pathway-level annotation)
  }
  # Step 2: keep only those with NO label in the NCBITaxon ontology graph
  FILTER NOT EXISTS {
    GRAPH <http://rdf-plantmetwiki.bioinformatics.nl/graph/ncbitaxon> {
      ?taxon rdfs:label ?label .
    }
  }
  # Step 3: look up entity type (GeneProduct / Protein) from the pathways graph
  # Uses UNION to handle both direct typing and DataNode → wp:isAbout indirection
  OPTIONAL {
    GRAPH <http://rdf-plantmetwiki.bioinformatics.nl/graph/pathways> {
      { ?dn wp:isAbout ?node ; a ?nodeType . }
      UNION
      { ?node a ?nodeType . }
      FILTER(STRSTARTS(STR(?nodeType), "http://vocabularies.wikipathways.org/wp#"))
      FILTER(?nodeType != wp:DataNode)
    }
  }
}
GROUP BY ?taxon
ORDER BY DESC(?nNodes)

examples.label: VoID metadata of the datasets
examples.description: Inspect the VoID metadata header describing all PlantMetWiki datasets. Shows dataset names, versions, triple counts, creation dates, clickable Zenodo deposit DOIs (foaf:page), and source provenance.

examples.label: BridgeDb cross-references per database
examples.description: Count how many wp:Metabolite nodes carry a BridgeDb-materialised cross-reference to each external chemical database. Shows the reach of the BridgeDb metabolite mapping in PlantMetWiki (release v3.2): e.g. Wikidata, PubChem and ChEBI each reach ~3,000 metabolites, up from a handful of source identifiers.

examples.label: Metabolite cross-references from BridgeDb
examples.description: List PlantMetWiki metabolites with the external cross-references materialised by BridgeDb (wp:bdb* predicates: ChEBI, Wikidata, PubChem, HMDB, KEGG, ...). These links are stored directly in the graph, so no federation is needed to resolve a metabolite to its ChEBI / Wikidata / PubChem entries.

examples.label: Pathways of a species, with data node counts
examples.description: Find all pathways containing DataNodes annotated for a given species, and count annotated DataNodes per pathway.

examples.label: Species with an enzyme for each reaction of a pathway
examples.description: Cross-species inference: for a given pathway, list every Conversion reaction and which species have an annotated enzyme (GeneProduct or Protein) that catalyses it.

examples.label: Genes and enzymes per species
examples.description: For every species annotated in PlantMetWiki, the number of gene products, proteins and pathways, sorted by the number of genes and proteins.
examples.query:
#   - number of distinct wp:GeneProduct DataNodes
#   - number of distinct wp:Protein DataNodes
#   - total gene/protein entities (nTotal)
#   - number of distinct pathways covered
# Results sorted by total entity count descending.
#
# Named graphs used:
#   graph/pathways            — DataNode types and pathway membership
#   graph/gpml-taxonomy-extra — wp:organism annotations per DataNode
#   graph/ncbitaxon           — taxon labels

PREFIX wp:      <http://vocabularies.wikipathways.org/wp#>
PREFIX rdfs:    <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#>
PREFIX dcterms: <http://purl.org/dc/terms/>
PREFIX ncbi:    <http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/NCBITaxon_>

SELECT ?taxon ?species
  (COUNT(DISTINCT ?gene)     AS ?nGenes)
  (COUNT(DISTINCT ?protein)  AS ?nProteins)
  (COUNT(DISTINCT ?pathway)  AS ?nPathways)
WHERE {
  # DataNode annotated to a specific species
  GRAPH <http://rdf-plantmetwiki.bioinformatics.nl/graph/gpml-taxonomy-extra> {
    ?entity wp:organism ?taxon .
    FILTER(?taxon != ncbi:33090)  # exclude pathway-level Viridiplantae
  }
  GRAPH <http://rdf-plantmetwiki.bioinformatics.nl/graph/ncbitaxon> {
    ?taxon rdfs:label ?species .
  }
  GRAPH <http://rdf-plantmetwiki.bioinformatics.nl/graph/pathways> {
    ?entity dcterms:isPartOf ?pathway .
    OPTIONAL { ?gene a wp:GeneProduct . FILTER(?gene = ?entity) }
    OPTIONAL { ?protein a wp:Protein . FILTER(?protein = ?entity) }
  }
}
GROUP BY ?taxon ?species
ORDER BY DESC(COUNT(DISTINCT ?entity))

examples.label: Number of interactions per type
examples.description: Count the number of interactions of each wp:Interaction subtype across the whole knowledge base: Catalysis, Conversion, TranscriptionTranslation, Inhibition, Stimulation, Binding and ComplexBinding.
examples.query:
#                   Stimulation, Binding, ComplexBinding.
#
# Named graphs used:
#   graph/pathways — all interaction triples

PREFIX wp:      <http://vocabularies.wikipathways.org/wp#>
PREFIX rdf:     <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#>

SELECT ?interactionType (COUNT(DISTINCT ?interaction) AS ?nInteractions)
WHERE {
  GRAPH <http://rdf-plantmetwiki.bioinformatics.nl/graph/pathways> {
    ?interaction rdf:type ?interactionType .
    VALUES ?interactionType {
      wp:Catalysis
      wp:Conversion
      wp:TranscriptionTranslation
      wp:Inhibition
      wp:Stimulation
      wp:Binding
      wp:ComplexBinding
    }
  }
}
GROUP BY ?interactionType
ORDER BY DESC(?nInteractions)

examples.label: Metabolite by PubChem ID, with its pathways and species
examples.description: Search PlantMetWiki starting from an external database identifier — here a PubChem Compound ID — and return the metabolite, its pathways and the species with annotated enzymes in those pathways.

examples.label: Metabolites in pathways of a species
examples.description: Find metabolites in pathways that contain DataNodes annotated for a given species. Because metabolites themselves are rarely species-specific, this query finds all metabolites that co-occur in pathways with the requested species' genes/proteins.

examples.label: Number of references per pathway
examples.description: Count the number of distinct publication references per pathway, sorted by most cited.

examples.label: Content of a pathway
examples.description: Summarise the content of a specific pathway by its stable PlantCyc PWY ID. Returns: pathway title, stable PWY ID, internal PC identifier, counts of each DataNode type (GeneProduct, Protein, Metabolite, Complex), number of distinct species, and number of Conversion reactions.

examples.label: Proteins in pathways of a taxon
examples.description: Find proteins in pathways for a given NCBI taxon ID. The taxonomy-extra graph annotates the biological entity IRI directly (the same IRI that carries rdf:type wp:Protein and dcterms:isPartOf in the pathways graph), so the join is simple: match ?protein across both graphs.

examples.label: Proteins of a pathway, with references
examples.description: List all proteins (with labels and publication references) for a given pathway.

examples.label: Species in a pathway
examples.description: Show all species (with NCBI taxon IDs and labels) present in a given pathway. Species are identified from DataNode-level annotations in the taxonomy-extra graph.
examples.query:
# Named graphs used:
#   graph/pathways            — pathway and DataNode triples
#   graph/gpml-taxonomy-extra — wp:organism annotations per DataNode
#   graph/ncbitaxon           — taxon labels
# Editable placeholder: change "/PC159_" to any other internal pathway ID fragment.

PREFIX wp:      <http://vocabularies.wikipathways.org/wp#>
PREFIX rdfs:    <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#>
PREFIX dc:      <http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/>
PREFIX dcterms: <http://purl.org/dc/terms/>
PREFIX ncbi:    <http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/NCBITaxon_>

SELECT DISTINCT ?taxonID ?species ?title
WHERE {
  # Find the pathway by internal sequential ID fragment
  GRAPH <http://rdf-plantmetwiki.bioinformatics.nl/graph/pathways> {
    ?pw dc:title ?title .
    FILTER(CONTAINS(STR(?pw), '/PC159_'))  # change pathway ID fragment here
    ?dataNode dcterms:isPartOf ?pw .
  }
  # Get species annotation on DataNodes in this pathway
  GRAPH <http://rdf-plantmetwiki.bioinformatics.nl/graph/gpml-taxonomy-extra> {
    ?dataNode wp:organism ?taxonID .
    FILTER(?taxonID != ncbi:33090)  # exclude pathway-level Viridiplantae
  }
  # Resolve taxon label
  GRAPH <http://rdf-plantmetwiki.bioinformatics.nl/graph/ncbitaxon> {
    ?taxonID rdfs:label ?species .
  }
}
ORDER BY ?species

examples.label: Title and DOI of the references of pathways with few references
examples.description: Pathways with at most two references, with the title and DOI of each reference from Wikidata (through QLever). Returns 10 pathways at a time (LIMIT and OFFSET).
examples.query:
PREFIX biopax:  <http://www.biopax.org/release/biopax-level3.owl#>
PREFIX cito:    <http://purl.org/spar/cito/>
PREFIX dc:      <http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/>
PREFIX dcterms: <http://purl.org/dc/terms/>
PREFIX foaf:    <http://xmlns.com/foaf/0.1/>
PREFIX freq:    <http://purl.org/cld/freq/>
PREFIX gpml:    <http://vocabularies.wikipathways.org/gpml#>
PREFIX owl:     <http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#>
PREFIX pav:     <http://purl.org/pav/>
PREFIX prov:    <http://www.w3.org/ns/prov#>
PREFIX rdf:     <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#>
PREFIX rdfs:    <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#>
PREFIX skos:    <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#>
PREFIX void:    <http://rdfs.org/ns/void#>
PREFIX wp:      <http://vocabularies.wikipathways.org/wp#>
PREFIX wprdf:   <http://rdf.wikipathways.org/>
PREFIX xsd:     <http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#>
PREFIX pmw:		<http://rdf-plantmetwiki.bioinformatics.nl/pathways/>
PREFIX ncbi:    <http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/NCBITaxon_>
PREFIX ro:		<http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_> 
PREFIX bioregistry: <https://bioregistry.io/mibig:> 

#Federated prefixes:
PREFIX wd: <http://www.wikidata.org/entity/>
PREFIX wdt: <http://www.wikidata.org/prop/direct/>
PREFIX p: <http://www.wikidata.org/prop/>
PREFIX pq: <http://www.wikidata.org/prop/qualifier/>
PREFIX wdtn: <http://www.wikidata.org/prop/direct-normalized/> 

SELECT DISTINCT ?pwID ?title ?nPublications ?paperTitle ?pubmedWD ?DOI ?wd
WHERE {  
  {
  
  SELECT ?pwID ?title ?pubmedWD (COUNT(DISTINCT ?pubmed) AS ?nPublications)
    WHERE {
  		?pw a wp:Pathway ;                #Define pathways
      		dc:title ?title ;             #Define pathway titles
      		dc:identifier ?pwID ;         #Define pathway IDs
      		(dcterms:references|cito:cites) ?pubmed .  #Collect total references for pathways
      
        ?pw (dcterms:references|cito:cites) ?pubmedWD .  #Keep PMIDs for downstream analysis
      
        }
    GROUP BY ?pwID ?title ?pubmedWD                   #Results need to be aggregated to apply count
    HAVING (COUNT(DISTINCT ?pubmed) <= 2)             #Retrieve pathways with a few publication
    LIMIT 10                                          #To avoid timeouts
    OFFSET 10                                         #To retrieve item 101-200, can be used in a script to collect data from all entries
    }
  
      BIND(STR(?pubmedWD) AS ?pubmedStr)
      BIND(STRAFTER(?pubmedStr, "https://identifiers.org/pubmed/") AS ?pmid0raw)
      
SERVICE <https://qlever.cs.uni-freiburg.de/api/wikidata> {
  ?wd wdt:P698 ?pmid0raw .                           #Connect PMID from pathways to Wikidata entries
      OPTIONAL{ ?wd wdtn:P356 ?DOI ;                 #If there is a DOI, extract
      wdt:P1476 ?paperTitle . }                      #If there is a title, extract
}
}
ORDER BY DESC (?nPublications) ?title

examples.label: IDSM chemical similarity search
examples.description: Finds structurally similar ChEBI compounds for source and target metabolites in a pathway's directed interactions via the IDSM/ChEBI structure search service (idsm.elixir-czech.cz). May be slower due to external endpoint dependency.
examples.query:
PREFIX owl: <http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#>
PREFIX ebi: <http://ebi.rdf.ac.uk/dataset/>
PREFIX sachem: <http://bioinfo.uochb.cas.cz/rdf/v1.0/sachem#>
PREFIX idsm: <https://idsm.elixir-czech.cz/sparql/endpoint/>
PREFIX dcterms: <http://purl.org/dc/terms/>
PREFIX wp: <http://vocabularies.wikipathways.org/wp#>
PREFIX sso: <http://semanticscience.org/resource/>
PREFIX rh:<http://rdf.rhea-db.org/>
PREFIX rdfs:<http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#>
PREFIX xsd:     <http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#>
SELECT distinct ((substr(str(?chebioSrc),32)) as ?SourceOrigin) ((substr(str(?similarSrc),32)) as ?SourceSimilar) ((substr(str(?chebioTgt),32)) as ?TargetOrigin) ((substr(str(?similarTgt),32)) as ?TargetSimilar)  #?reaction
WHERE {
  ?interaction dcterms:isPartOf ?pathway ; a wp:Conversion ;
      wp:source ?source ;
      wp:target ?target .
    ?source wp:bdbChEBI ?chebiSrc .
    ?target wp:bdbChEBI ?chebiTgt .
    VALUES ?pathwayId { "PC302" }
    ?pathway dcterms:identifier ?pathwayId.
    BIND(iri(concat("http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_", substr(str(?chebiSrc),37))) AS ?chebioSrc)
    BIND(iri(concat("http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_", substr(str(?chebiTgt),37))) AS ?chebioTgt)
#IDSM
SERVICE <https://idsm.elixir-czech.cz/sparql/endpoint/chebi> {
   ?chebioSrc ^sso:is-attribute-of / sso:has-value ?molfileSrc .
 ?chebioTgt ^sso:is-attribute-of / sso:has-value ?molfileTgt .
  [ sachem:compound ?similarSrc; sachem:score ?scoreSrc ]
    sachem:similaritySearch [
      sachem:query ?molfileSrc ;
     sachem:cutoff 98e-2
    ].
  [ sachem:compound ?similarTgt; sachem:score ?scoreTgt ]
    sachem:similaritySearch [
      sachem:query ?molfileTgt ;
      sachem:cutoff 98e-2
    ] .
  }
 }

examples.label: Wikidata, ChEBI and PubChem for metabolites, by InChIKey
examples.description: Retrieve Wikidata entries, ChEBI IDs, and PubChem CIDs for metabolites in PlantMetWiki, matched via InChIKey (wdt:P235). Returns metabolites that occur in at most one pathway (rare/specialised compounds).

examples.label: Pathways and species of metabolites, by InChIKey
examples.description: Find pathways and associated plant species for specific metabolites of interest, identified by their InChIKey. Enriches results with Wikidata entry and label.

examples.label: Pathways and species of metabolites, by name
examples.description: Find metabolites by name, list the pathways they appear in, and which plant species are annotated in those pathways (via DataNode-level taxonomy, not pathway-level wp:organismName). Also enriches each metabolite with Wikidata active ingredient info (federated query).

examples.label: SMILES from Wikidata for metabolites of a species
examples.description: Retrieve metabolites (with InChIKey and SMILES) from pathways that have a specific species annotated at the DataNode level, enriched via Wikidata federated query. Species filtering uses graph/gpml-taxonomy-extra + graph/ncbitaxon (NOT wp:organismName, which only returns "Viridiplantae" at pathway level).

examples.label: Rhea Reaction Enrichment
examples.description: For a pathway's reactions that carry a Rhea cross-reference, federates to the Rhea SPARQL endpoint (sparql.rhea-db.org) to retrieve the full reaction equation and every participating ChEBI compound. Returns one row per (reaction, Rhea participant) to avoid GROUP_CONCAT overflow.

examples.label: UniProt GO Enrichment
examples.description: For a pathway's enzymes that carry a UniProt accession, federates to UniProt's own SPARQL endpoint (sparql.uniprot.org) to retrieve every Gene Ontology (GO) term the enzyme is annotated with — molecular function, biological process and cellular component alike. PlantMetWiki itself carries no GO annotations at all; this is the live bridge to them.

examples.label: ENZYME Nomenclature Enrichment
examples.description: For a pathway's reactions that carry an "Enzyme Nomenclature" (EC number) cross-reference, federates to UniProt's own SPARQL endpoint (sparql.uniprot.org) — which also serves the Expasy ENZYME database in RDF — to retrieve the enzyme's official name, synonyms and curator comments (catalytic notes, substrate range, species specificity).

examples.label: SwissLipids Enrichment
examples.description: For a pathway's metabolites identified by InChIKey, federates to the SwissLipids SPARQL endpoint (beta.sparql.swisslipids.org) to check whether the compound is a registered lipid species, returning its SwissLipids name and equivalent ChEBI class. Matches both lipids proper (fatty acyl-CoAs, phospholipids, ...) and shared cofactors SwissLipids also curates (ATP, CoA, NAD(P)(H), water, diphosphate) because they appear in lipid-metabolism reactions too.

examples.label: PROSITE / HAMAP Domain Signatures
examples.description: For a pathway's UniProt-accession enzymes, federates to UniProt's own SPARQL endpoint to list the PROSITE pattern/profile and HAMAP family signature identifiers (rdfs:seeAlso) attached to each protein. LIMITATION (checked live, both still true as of writing): neither PROSITE nor HAMAP currently exposes a reachable public SPARQL endpoint of their own (purl.expasy.org/prosite/signature/<id> resolves to an HTML page only; HAMAP's documented endpoint, hamap.expasy.org/sparql[/sparql], 404s on every URL pattern tried), so this query can only surface the bare signature id via UniProt — not the signature's name/description, which would need a second federated hop that isn't available right now.
